intervals.label: physics runs
intervals.locator: arXiv:2312.17573, Introduction (first physics run in 2023 with a Xe beam); 64th PAC PP report: ninth physics run recorded 2.75 billion events
intervals.note: The detector paper dates the "first physics run" to 2023 with a xenon beam; earlier runs with carbon, argon and krypton beams exist (the Lambda paper uses carbon-beam data) but their dates are not in the sources fetched, so the start is the earliest documented run. The June 2026 report counts a ninth physics run (Xe + Sn, 2.75 billion events) after an eighth run (Xe + CsI).
intervals.quote: A schematic view of the BM@N setup, as used in the first physics run in 2023 with a Xe beam, is shown in Fig. 1.

placements.quote: BM@N (Baryonic Matter at Nuclotron) is the first experiment operational at the Nuclotron/NICA ion-accelerating complex, dedicated to studying interactions of relativistic beams of heavy ions with fixed targets

summary.plain: A forward magnetic spectrometer with a large dipole magnet, silicon and gas tracking, time-of-flight and calorimeters that records the particles produced when heavy ions hit a fixed target.
summary.technical: BM@N forward spectrometer (1.6 < eta < 4.4): SP-41 analysing magnet (3.15 Tm at 2000 A), beam and trigger detectors, silicon and GEM tracking, drift/cathode-strip chambers, TOF400/TOF700 walls, calorimetry.

technology.quote: The BM@N detector is a forward spectrometer that covers the pseudorapidity range 1.6 ≤ η ≤ 4.4.
technology.value: Forward magnetic spectrometer with a dipole magnet, beam monitoring, tracking, time-of-flight and calorimeters
